title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Duty of Candour - Binding Authority
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: During a Small Claims Court trial, a paralegal realizes that a recent, binding Divisional Court decision directly contradicts their client's legal argument. Opposing counsel, who is self-represented, is unaware of this decision. What is the paralegal's ethical obligation?
options: Keep quiet about the decision, as the paralegal has a duty of zealous advocacy to their client.
Disclose the binding decision to the judge, even though it is detrimental to their client's case.
Wait for the judge to find the decision independently, but do not actively conceal it.
Withdraw from the representation because the case no longer has merit.
questions.explain: Rule 2.01 (Duty to the Administration of Justice) dictates that an advocate must act with candour. This includes an affirmative obligation to bring to the tribunal's attention any binding authority that is directly on point, regardless of whether it supports or damages the client's case.
